name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention; accurately describes 'get character base table entry'. No Ghidra address residue. char_base = the per-character starting-attribute table (24-byte stride, 32 playable-character entries), matching KB struct char_base_entry (人物出場屬性, 24 bytes).
purpose: Leaf accessor that returns a pointer to character_base_table[idx], the per-character starting-attribute table (one 24-byte entry per playable character).
logic_summary: Pure index-to-pointer: returns &data_fd2_battle_character_base_table[idx], i.e. EAX = idx*0x18 + 0x61DA1. Standard EBP frame, 1 stack arg, no side effects, no callees. Entry layout (24B): bRA(+0) bCL(+1) bLV(+2) wHP(+3,u16) wMP(+5,u16) bMV(+7) pMG[4](+8 spell bitmap) pIT[6](+0xC item ids, 0xFF=empty) wAP(+0x12,u16) wDP(+0x14,u16) wDX(+0x16,u16).

params.name: idx
params.semantics: char_id (0..0x1F = 32 playable characters). Used as table index: idx*0x18 + base. This is a meaningful domain ID (character id), must be preserved.
params.reason: Descriptive index name; no address residue. Both callers (fd2_init_runtime_char_for_battle, fd2_init_runtime_char_from_base_growth) pass a char_id, so 'idx' is appropriate and accurate.

returns.semantics: Pointer to the idx-th character_base_table entry's first byte (bRA field at +0). Callers cast it and read base stats/equipment, combining with char_growth scaled by level to build a runtime char slot.

comment_original_issue: Original src comment ('Returns pointer to character_base_table[idx].') was correct but terse: it did not state the index domain (char_id 0..0x1F, 32 entries) or the entry layout that callers rely on.
notes: Ghidra plate already exhaustive and accurate (full struct layout, 9-inst body, both callers); src comment now a consistent precis, so plate left unchanged. File header (lines 1-8) says '13 leaf functions' / address range 0x4E48D..0x4E7F8, but the file also contains fd2_get_orphan_table_60181_entry @ 0x4DB84 (14 functions, range extends below 0x4E48D); not touched per single-symbol scope (out of this symbol's comment block). KB sample LE addr for char_base_entry is 0x55BA1 vs this build's 0x61DA1 -- expected per-build address drift; 24-byte stride is the stable anchor and matches exactly.
